items.cap: "The day of the decease: On 11th December 1947 " — died at 85 Rheeden St, Forest Hill , Johannesburg.

items.alt: Detail showing age 46 years 6 months and occupation S.A.R. and H.
items.cap: Age 46 years 6 months ; occupation S.A.R. & H. — the South African Railways and Harbours; residence 85 Rheeden Street, Forest Hill .

items.alt: Detail showing surviving spouse Gertruida Alexandra born Kinnear and pre-deceased spouse Anna Johanna Maria born Pretorius.
items.cap: Surviving spouse Gertruida Alexandra Booyzen, born Kinnear , in community of property; pre-deceased spouse Anna Johanna Maria Booyzen (Pretorius), died 26 February 1944 .

items.alt: Detail listing the children of the prior marriage with birth dates for the minors.
items.cap: Children of the prior marriage. The two eldest are entered as majors; the four minors carry birth dates — 25/3/29, 12/10/30, 22/9/32, 10/1/34 — which match the tree exactly , independently confirming Catherine Mary Sophia's birth on 25 March 1929. The second daughter is given a married name the tree does not have: Kelly .

items.alt: Two men shaking hands in open grassland, one young in a 1930s suit, one elderly with a white moustache and walking stick.
items.cap: "George Booyzen and Isaak Pretorius In Transkei" — the tree's own caption. Left: George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen , in his thirties, in the wide trousers of the 1930s. Right: Isaak Pretorius , a relative of George's wife, walking stick planted in the grass behind him. This appears to be the only photograph of George in the tree — his profile still carries MyHeritage's prompt to add a personal photo.

items.alt: A young woman in a patterned dress, an elderly woman seated in black, and a young man outside a house.
items.cap: An elderly woman seated in full black between two young people, outside a plastered house. Hypothesis: the seated woman is Kathleen Barry (1859–1940) in widow's black — the dress and print date the image to the 1930s, when she was in her seventies and living in Johannesburg. Unverified.

items.alt: A young man in a dark uniform tunic and peaked cap standing in a yard by a bare tree.
items.cap: A young man in a dark uniform tunic and peaked cap . Hypothesis: George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen in South African Railways and Harbours uniform — the employer his 1947 death notice names. Unverified.

items.alt: A man in a light suit and fedora leaning on a late-1920s sedan with a small boy beside him.
items.cap: A man in a light suit and fedora on a late-1920s sedan, registration TAS 486 , a small boy beside him. The registration is a hard, researchable detail. Unidentified.

items.alt: Blackletter heading reading This is the last Will and Testament, with a marginal note naming John Gottlob Kolbe.
items.cap: " This is the last Will and Testament of me John Gottlob Kolbe of Conduit Street, Bond Street , in the County…"

items.alt: Dense register-hand page of the will naming trustees and the partnership.
items.cap: "…of Middlesex Tailor I give devise and bequeath all my Estate both Real and Personal … unto Timothy Duke of Lombard Street, Gentleman, Christian William Kent of Bentinck Street, Poland Street, Tailor, and my daughter Marian Kolbe … upon Trust ."

items.alt: Closing page of the will carrying the probate act clause.
items.cap: The closing page and the probate act — proved at London, 23 February 1846 , three months after his burial at the Savoy.

items.alt: Page of the will setting out the residue clause and division among children.
items.cap: The residue: "… unto for and amongst all and every my child and children who may be living at the time of my decease in equal shares … and the issue of such of my children respectively as may be dead , such issue however to take only the share to which their parent would have been entitled."

items.alt: Final page of the will with signature, witnesses and the probate act.
items.cap: Signed "J. G. Kolbe" , 25 May 1842, "written in one sheet of paper". Witnessed by Wm Gribble Jr and another, described as "Clerks to Mr Duke, Lombard Street" — the executor's own clerks. PROVED at London the 23rd February 1846 before Herbert Thomas Pratt, Doctor of Laws and Surrogate.
